summary: Attacked part 1 of the Number fields and class field theory area — ArithmeticGaloisDuality, GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic, HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory, tauceti:Completed/EffectiveBounds, tauceti:Completed/IntegralLattices, tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory, 61 stages, with 60 accepted paper routes landing on the first three. Two findings, both medium. First, the area's most heavily routed roadmap opens by naming three roadmaps to reuse and records none of them in any machine-readable field, on either side, while two sibling roadmaps in the same area declare every owner they name in prose and are reciprocated by all of them. Second, the normalized Siegel series and its functional equation, which five accepted extractions route into a single stage, are named by no layer anywhere in the atlas and exist in neither library. The heads that came back clean are recorded with their evidence, including a declaration-level verification of both archived roadmaps' completion claims, which hold.
checked: Every stage of all seven roadmaps: ClassFieldTheory 15, Chebotarev 14, ArithmeticGaloisDuality 8, HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory 8, GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic 7, tauceti:Completed/IntegralLattices 5, tauceti:Completed/EffectiveBounds 4 — 61 in all, with the roadmap documents for the two archived roadmaps read in full.

Eligibility, measured rather than assumed, and one disclosure. Of the papers this session has reviewed, exactly one routes here: PAPER-NAKAMURA-23 to ArithmeticGaloisDuality. I reviewed that extraction (I did not write it), the target of this job is the area rather than that paper, and no finding below rests on the Nakamura routing or on any judgement I made reviewing it.

The 60 paper routes, at route granularity rather than by substring: GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic 33, ArithmeticGaloisDuality 24, HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory 3, and 0 to the four tauceti-origin roadmaps. All 60 are `source` routes. I read every route reason, and the stage distribution: GN.3 receives 14, the most of any stage in the area, then R02.4 with 11, GN.2 with 10, R02.2 and GN.4 with 9. Seven stages receive none, six of them in HigherLocalFields plus ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D8.

Why the stage-level graph and status differ across the area, which also answers a question part 2 left open. The three campaign-origin roadmaps carry all 38 stage `requires` edges and status `needs_source_decomposition`; the four tauceti-origin ones carry 0 edges and `unknown`. Empty stage edges track a roadmap's origin, not the attention an area has had, so they are not a finding for either part. The same holds at roadmap level: campaign-origin roadmaps declare a prerequisite in 147 of 151 cases (97 per cent), tauceti-origin in 14 of 60 (23 per cent).

The mechanism behind the `prerequisites` field, established before using it as evidence: for each of the three campaign roadmaps, `prerequisites` equals or contains exactly the set of roadmaps its stages reach by a cross-roadmap `requires` edge. So the field tracks stage edges, and a reuse relation stated only in prose, which never became a stage edge, is invisible in every machine-readable field. That is the defect class of the first finding.

ArithmeticGaloisDuality's ownership discipline, which is exemplary and is the contrast case that makes the first finding a finding. Its summary names four upstream owners and says what it will not rebuild — 'ProfiniteCohomology owns the canonical continuous cohomology object ... ClassFieldTheory already owns local Tate duality for finite modules ... Neither is rebuilt here' — and D7 adds 'Local Tate duality for finite modules remains upstream ClassFieldTheory' and assigns Selmer conditions to SelmerIwasawaCohomology and the cyclotomic comparison to PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology. All four named owners appear in its `prerequisites`, two of them (ClassFieldTheory, ProfiniteCohomology) with no stage edge at all, and all four reciprocate: each lists ArithmeticGaloisDuality in its `consumers`. Four for four.

HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory against the same test, which it also passes. Its summary says 'Reuse the existing symbol/norm-residue and duality owners', and its `prerequisites` are K2SymbolsBrauer, MotivicEtaleKTheory and SchemeAndStackFoundations — which are, exactly, the only three roadmaps in either directory that cite it. Its `consumers: []` is correct rather than an omission: nothing downstream consumes higher class field theory yet, so it is a leaf. Six of its eight stages receive no paper route, which for a proposed frontier roadmap is expected and not a finding.

Both archived roadmaps' completion claims, verified at declaration level against the real library trees rather than taken on trust, because a roadmap marked complete that the library does not support would outrank anything else here. tauceti:Completed/EffectiveBounds declares 'Status: declared complete by the maintainers (2026-07-02) ... This roadmap is archived' and names five declarations as landed: abs_discr_le_of_basis_isIntegral, classNumber_le_bound, units_sq_index_le, card_ideal_absNorm_le and the Layer-2 summit ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_le. All five are present in Tau Ceti, its two named directories under TauCeti/NumberTheory/ (EffectiveBounds and GeometryOfNumbers) exist, and they contain no `sorry`. tauceti:Completed/IntegralLattices states its completion criterion instead — 'complete only when the general APIs, all table rows, and the D8 subset E8 isometry have been formalized' — and that is met: TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ has 38 files and no `sorry`, including RootLattice/D8Plus/Isometry.lean and Examples.lean, with 21 files mentioning a discriminant group and 12 an overlattice. Both markings are justified.

Three leads inside that check which dissolved, recorded so a verifier need not repeat them. (1) EffectiveBounds' stage descriptions read as an open migration plan — 'the migration candidate', 'Before porting', 'the first migration targets', 'What is missing is the effective side' — which looked like a lifecycle contradicting its own text; it is retained plan text in an archived roadmap whose document declares completion, so there is no contradiction. (2) Searching for HermiteMinkowski returned 0 files in both libraries and looked like the summit being absent; the declaration is named ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_le and is present, which is why absence-by-name is not evidence. (3) GeometricCore and index_powMonoidHom_two_le_of_closure are both absent from Tau Ceti, but the document names them as files and lemmas in the external erdos migration *source*, never as landed targets, so neither is an overclaim.

A tooling trap of my own, hit twice, recorded because it produced false cleans that agreed with what I expected. My first library probe pointed at a .lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib path inside the Tau Ceti checkout, which does not exist there; the second used a tree holding one .lean file. Both returned 0 for every search. The real trees are a full Mathlib checkout (8556 .lean files) and the Tau Ceti library tree (5268), and every library number in this red team comes from those. Printing the tree's file count beside each result is what caught it.

Duplication across the two parts of the area, read from this side. The quadratic-forms pair is the one at risk: GN.2 'Quadratic and hermitian local-global theory' covers Witt groups, discriminants, Clifford and Hasse invariants, local classification and Hasse-Minkowski, which is part 2's GlobalQuadraticForms (finite-place invariants, Hasse-Minkowski isotropy, Witt consequences) and QuadraticFormInvariants. The intent is reuse, not duplication — GN's summary says so in its first sentence and GN.2's distinctive content is the integral and hermitian layer (integral lattices, genera, spinor genera, quaternionic and hermitian variants) that part 2 does not plan. So no mathematics is planned twice, but nothing records the relation either, which is the first finding. This also corrects a statement in my own part-2 red team, that the division across the parts is 'by object and not by theorem, part 2 forms over fields and part 1 lattices over Z': GN.2 covers Hasse-Minkowski and Witt groups over fields, and GN.6 is Hermitian K-theory and Grothendieck-Witt groups, which is neither. The accurate statement is that part 1 reuses part 2's field theory and adds the integral and hermitian layer.

The library boundary for the quadratic-form material, against the real trees: QuadraticForm appears in 42 Mathlib files and 158 Tau Ceti files, while HasseMinkowski, hasseInvariant, WittRing and WittGroup return 0 in both, and spinorNorm or spinorGenus returns 0 in Mathlib and 2 in Tau Ceti. The last independently confirms the premise of the PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20 route, which says its work is 'built on Tau Ceti's spinor norm over fields'.

findings.where: research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic.json — the roadmap-level `prerequisites` field, and the `consumers` field of the roadmaps it names
findings.claim: GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic opens its summary by naming three roadmaps it depends on — 'Reuse QuadraticFormInvariants, GlobalQuadraticForms and AdelicAlgebraicGroups' — and records none of them anywhere machine-readable: not in its `prerequisites`, not in any of its 15 `stageEdges`, not in any stage's `requires`, and not on the supplier side, where both GlobalQuadraticForms and QuadraticFormInvariants have `consumers: []`. A fourth relation is missing the same way: several accepted paper routes instruct workers to import tauceti:Completed/IntegralLattices ('do not re-plan the completed lattice roadmap'), and that roadmap, which this red team verified is built and sorry-free, also records `consumers: []`. This is the area's most heavily routed roadmap, taking 33 of the 60 routes, so the ordering is load-bearing. It is not a house style: two sibling roadmaps in the same area and the same origin class declare every owner they name in prose, and are reciprocated.
findings.evidence: The summary of research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic.json begins: 'Reuse QuadraticFormInvariants, GlobalQuadraticForms and AdelicAlgebraicGroups. General homogeneous-dynamics theorems are separate substantial source developments, not corollaries of Minkowski.' Its `prerequisites` is ['ClassicalArithmeticCompletion', 'GeneralAlgebraicKTheory'] — exactly the two roadmaps its stages reach by a cross-roadmap `requires` edge (ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.3, GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4:construction, GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.6). None of the three summary-named roadmaps appears in that field, in any `requires`, or in any of its 15 stageEdges; and tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_GlobalQuadraticForms.json and tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_QuadraticFormInvariants.json both have `consumers: []`. The contrast cases, in the same area: ArithmeticGaloisDuality names four owners in prose ('ProfiniteCohomology owns the canonical continuous cohomology object ... ClassFieldTheory already owns local Tate duality for finite modules ... Neither is rebuilt here') and declares all four in `prerequisites` — ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations, SelmerIwasawaCohomology, tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory, tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology — of which the last two have no stage edge whatever, and all four list ArithmeticGaloisDuality in their own `consumers`. HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory likewise says 'Reuse the existing symbol/norm-residue and duality owners' and declares K2SymbolsBrauer, MotivicEtaleKTheory and SchemeAndStackFoundations. The consequence has teeth rather than being bookkeeping alone: GN.2's instruction is 'Construct and export. Integrate Witt groups, discriminants, Clifford/Hasse invariants, local classification and Hasse-Minkowski; add integral lattices, genera, spinor genera and quaternionic/hermitian variants', and Witt groups, Clifford and Hasse invariants, local classification and Hasse-Minkowski are precisely what GlobalQuadraticForms and QuadraticFormInvariants plan, so the single summary sentence is all that stands between a worker and building them twice.
findings.fix: Declare the relations on both sides, as this area already does elsewhere. Add tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/QuadraticFormInvariants, tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalQuadraticForms, AdelicAlgebraicGroups and tauceti:Completed/IntegralLattices to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic's `prerequisites`, and add GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic to each of those four roadmaps' `consumers`, matching the reciprocity ArithmeticGaloisDuality and its four owners already keep. No stage edge is required for this — ClassFieldTheory and ProfiniteCohomology are declared by ArithmeticGaloisDuality without one — so the fix is additive and creates no cycle. If a stage-level record is wanted as well, the natural edges are from GN.2 to the GlobalQuadraticForms and QuadraticFormInvariants layers that supply Hasse-Minkowski and the local invariants, and from GN.2 to IntegralLattices for the discriminant and gluing operations the paper routes name.

findings.where: GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.3 (Reduction, mass and theta series), and the atlas as a whole
findings.claim: Five accepted paper extractions route the normalized Siegel series and the machinery around it into GN.3 and nowhere else, and no layer in the atlas names it. GN.3 owns 'local representation densities' — the density half — but never mentions the Siegel series, its functional equation, or the weighted lattice counts the papers actually need; and a search of both roadmap directories for 'Siegel series' returns no file at all. Neither library has it either, so this is mathematics the area's routed papers depend on that nothing plans and nothing supplies. GN.3 is also the most heavily routed stage in the area, taking 14 of 60 routes while bundling reduction domains, arithmetic quotients, densities, mass formulas and theta-series interfaces, so the granularity is part of the problem.
findings.evidence: The five papers and their mentions of 'Siegel series': PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24 (11), PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B (10), PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22 (6), PAPER-LI-LIU-22 (3), PAPER-HE-LI-SHI-ETAL-23 (1); every one routes to GN.3 and to no other stage, and none was written or reviewed by this session. Their route reasons name the material precisely: 'the normalized Siegel series Den(X, L) with its functional equation and cancellation laws'; 'the normalized local Siegel series in odd and even corank, with Ikeda's functional equations and the induction formula'; 'the Cho-Yamauchi weighted lattice count, with its finite-field iso[metry counts]'; 'the closed formula of Theorem 7.1 for the modified derivative of primitive densities'; and PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24 routes the Hermitian case 'in the form needed for Siegel series'. GN.3's own text is: 'Reduction, mass and theta series. Construct and export. Construct reduction domains and arithmetic quotients, local representation densities, mass formulas and theta-series interfaces.' A case-insensitive search for 'Siegel series' across research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/ and research/blueprint/roadmaps/ returns 0 files. The only neighbouring owner, GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7, merely consumes the material — 'the finite-place identities between CM intersection multiplicities and derivatives of local representation densities/Whittaker functions' — and does not own it. Against the real library trees (Mathlib 8556 files, Tau Ceti 5268): SiegelSeries or siegelSeries 0 and 0, representationDensity or localDensity 0 and 0, massFormula or genusMass 0 and 0, Whittaker 1 and 0.
findings.fix: Give the Siegel series a named owner at the granularity the five papers route to. The economical fix is to split GN.3, which currently carries five distinct subjects, and give the normalized local Siegel series its own stage: the series Den(X, L) attached to a lattice, its relation to the local representation density, the functional equation and cancellation and induction laws, and the Cho-Yamauchi weighted lattice count with the finite-field isometry counts it reduces to, in both the quadratic and the unramified and ramified Hermitian cases the papers supply. If the material is judged too large for one stage of this roadmap — five papers supplying functional equations, corank inductions and derivative formulas suggests it is — then it belongs in a Part II for local densities and Siegel series, downstream of GN.2 and feeding GN.3's mass formulas and GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7. Either way the owning layer should name the Siegel series explicitly, so that the five routes point at a target that mentions what they carry.
